neutral_facts.value: The accused, including Rakesh Mishra, were involved in granting building and completion certificates to a hotel and club without proper approvals. The original building permission was granted to the applicant, and later a revised plan was submitted. The revised plan involved significant changes from the original plan, including increased built-up area for the hotel and decreased for the club. The accused granted the revision without approval from any committee and accepted honorary membership in the club. The prosecution alleged that these actions constituted illegal gratification and misuse of authority. The High Court set aside the order of framing charges, but the Supreme Court restored the order, finding sufficient material to make out a prima facie case against the accused.

prosecution_argument.value: The State argued that the High Court traversed beyond the permissible limit while deciding the legality of the order framing charges, being a pre-trial stage, and that only the charge-sheet along with the accompanying material should be considered at the stage of framing of charges.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that G.S. Jadon cannot be held liable for any act/omission done prior to or after his period of service as Building Officer, and that the revision jurisdiction of the High Court also includes the inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.PC.

quotes.text: Learned counsel appearing for the accused persons has argued that G.S. Jadon was in the office of Building Officer from 31.10.1994 to 16.10.1996. He cannot be held liable for any act/omission done prior to or after this period
It is contended that the revision jurisdiction of the High Court also includes the inherent jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr.PC

legal_principle_applied.value: The Court applied the principle that only the charge-sheet along with the accompanying material is to be considered at the stage of framing of charges, so as to satisfy whether a prima facie case is made out, and that it has to be the subjective satisfaction of the Court framing charges.
